Criminal Case No. 34754 of 2024

Sukhram Kulhare
 Versus
 The State Of Madhya Pradesh

Appearance:
 Shri Amit Dubey - Advocate for applicant.
Shri C.M. Tiwari - Government Advocate for State.

Order 
This is the first bail application filed on behalf of the applicant/accused under Section 482 of BNSS,
2023 for grant of anticipatory bail, as he is under apprehension of his arrest, in connection with Crime No. 106/2024, registered at Police Station Kohefiza, District Bhopal (M.P.) for the offences punishable under Sections 420, 467, 468, 471 and 120-B of the IPC.
2. As per prosecution story, the allegation against the applicant is that he has made forged and fabricated birth certificate.
Therefore, the aforesaid offence has been registered against the applicant.
3. Learned counsel appearing for the applicant submitted that applicant is innocent.
He has been made accused only on the basis of NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-JBP:40378 2 MCRC-34754-2024 memorandum of co-accused person Sonika Singh.
Co-accused Sonika Singh has falsely implicated the applicant only to save herself.
He has not made any birth certificate in fact co-accused herself received the birth certificate from someone else and believing the same as genuine, the same has been presented before the Court.
In these circumstances, applicant may be granted anticipatory bail.
4. Learned counsel for the State has opposed the grant of anticipatory bail to the applicant.
It is submitted that applicant has made forged birth certificate of Abhimanyu and Divya Singh and after receiving Rs.1200/-, he had given forged birth certificates to other co-accused person.

Thereafter,
co-accused Sonika Singh presented these birth certificates before the Court for financial gains in the Court proceedings and on the basis of these documents got an order of the Court in her favour.
It is Sukhram Kulhare vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 14 August, 2024

1 also submitted that Municipal Corporation has given information through its letter that these birth certificates have not been issued from its Office.
Co-accused Sonika Singh has returned these birth certificates to the present applicant and, therefore, these birth certificates are to be seized from the applicant.
Custodial interrogation is also required from the applicant.

In view of the above,
anticipatory bail may not be granted to the present applicant.

5 . From perusal of record and case diary, it is found that NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2024:MPHC-JBP:40378 3 MCRC-34754-2024 present applicant has made false birth certificate of Abhimanyu Singh and Divya Singh bearing registration No. 03162811262130 and 03162811262131 respectively and given it to other co-accused person.
Under Right to Information Act, it was informed by Municipal Corporation vide letter No.491 dated 13.02.2020 that these birth certificates have not been issued by its Office.
Therefore, looking to seriousness of offence, I am of the view that it is not a fit case for grant of anticipatory bail to the applicant.
6. Consequently, this first application under Section 482 of BNSS, 2023 for grant of anticipatory bail filed on behalf of applicant stands dismissed.

(PRAMOD KUMAR AGRAWAL) JUDGE shahina Sukhram Kulhare vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 14 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/53861181/
